I read all four differing files in both trees (via a full diff) and the two workspace source classes. Here is my plan.

## What differs (workspace → reference)

- `/workspace/src/packaging/dependency_groups.py` vs `/megabit/.megabit_ref/src/packaging/dependency_groups.py`: the reference adds a small method to the `CyclicDependencyGroup` error class (defined at line 36 in the workspace file) that tells Python how to rebuild the error. The workspace class only has its three-input setup method (line 43: `requested_group`, `group`, `include_group`) and no rebuild method.
- `/workspace/src/packaging/metadata.py` vs `/megabit/.megabit_ref/src/packaging/metadata.py`: the reference adds the same kind of rebuild method to the `InvalidMetadata` error class (defined at line 45 in the workspace file, with a two-input setup method at line 51: `field`, `message`). The workspace class has no rebuild method.
- `/workspace/tests/test_dependency_groups.py` vs reference: the reference adds one test that copies a `CyclicDependencyGroup` error by saving and reloading it and checks the three stored names (`requested_group`, `group`, `include_group`) and the message stay the same.
- `/workspace/tests/test_metadata.py` vs reference: the reference adds one test class that copies an `InvalidMetadata` error the same way and checks the stored field name and message stay the same.

No other files differ (the `.git` entry is just the workspace being a git checkout).

## What is missing/wrong for the user today

Both error classes store the details a caller needs (`CyclicDependencyGroup` keeps the requested group, the group, and the included group; `InvalidMetadata` keeps the field name and message). But when the error is copied the ordinary way Python copies things — saving it to a file, sending it between processes, or putting it in a cache — reloading it fails, because the saved information only has the finished message text and nothing that can rebuild the error the way it was made. The two new tests in the reference show exactly this scenario: copy the error out and back, and expect the fields and message to be identical. The reference makes that work.

## Hints (workspace paths only)

- `/workspace/src/packaging/dependency_groups.py`
- `/workspace/src/packaging/metadata.py`

## Planned ticket structure

- Title: about errors from dependency groups and metadata not surviving being copied.
- What happens now: copying these errors out and back fails to restore them; the details are lost / reload errors.
- What should happen: a copied error comes back with the same field names and same message.
- About this project: `packaging` is a library that helps tools read and check Python package information; these two errors are raised when dependency-group data or metadata is bad.
- Problem this solves: people who send errors between processes or store them hit a confusing failure instead of being able to keep or re-raise the original error with its details.
- What changed: the two error classes can now be copied out and restored; two new checks cover it.
- Impact: correctness and usability for anyone passing these errors around.
- User experience: today copying the error breaks it; after the change the copy looks the same as the original.
- Hints: the two workspace source paths above.

{"file_path": "/megabit/ticket.md", "content": "# Errors from dependency groups and metadata break when they are copied

## What happens now

Two of the errors this library raises keep useful details inside them. The cyclic dependency group error keeps the group that was asked for, the group it was found in, and the group it pointed to. The invalid metadata error keeps the name of the field that was wrong. But when one of these errors is saved away and read back — for example written to a file, sent to another program, or stored in a cache — the saved copy cannot be turned back into the same error. The details are dropped and reloading fails.

## What should happen

A person who saves one of these errors and reads it back should get the same error again. The group names and the field name should still be there, and the message should read exactly the same as before. This should work the same way for both errors.

## About this project

This project is a library that helps other tools read and check information about Python packages. It knows how to read package version numbers, requirements, dependency groups, and package metadata, and it tells the caller when something is wrong by raising errors. People building packaging tools use it so they do not have to write all of that checking themselves.

## Problem this solves

When an error is passed between programs or kept for later, it has to survive being copied. Today it does not, so people lose the reason the error happened and cannot show the original message or the group and field details to whoever needs them. This makes it hard to log errors properly or hand them from a worker to the main program.

## What changed

Both errors now come back whole after being saved and read again. The cyclic dependency group error keeps its three group names, and the invalid metadata error keeps the field name it was raised for. The messages stay the same. Two new checks were added, one for each error, that save the error out, read it back, and compare the details and the message.

## Impact

Correctness and ease of use when errors are copied.

## User experience

Before: a person catches the cyclic dependency group error, saves it, reads it back, and the restored error no longer knows which groups were involved, so they cannot re-show the original message. After: they do the same thing and the restored error has the same three group names and the same message as the one they caught. The same holds for the invalid metadata error and its field name.

## Hints

- /workspace/src/packaging/dependency_groups.py
- /workspace/src/packaging/metadata.py"}
